name: chaos-substrate
description: Knowledge-graph code memory for multi-repository projects. Six MCP tools: chaos_index (full index), chaos_reindex (hash-gated re-run), chaos_add (index git changes), chaos_feature (answer a feature question from the index with code excerpts, no source reads), chaos_compose (feature website), chaos_correlations (intra- and cross-repo feature links). Rust, TypeScript, JavaScript, Python, Solidity, GraphQL, Markdown; Postgres + pgvector; Ollama or OpenAI embeddings.

interface.shortDescription: Index repositories once, then answer feature questions from memory instead of re-reading source.
interface.longDescription: Chaos Substrate builds a persistent knowledge graph of one or more repositories (tree-sitter extraction, contextual chunks, real embeddings, feature communities) in Postgres + pgvector and exposes six tools over MCP: index, reindex, add, feature, compose, correlations. After indexing, agents ask `chaos_feature` and get token-bounded answers with exact code excerpts, run `chaos_add` after edits, write a clickable feature website with `chaos_compose`, and link features across the repos of a chaos.toml project with `chaos_correlations`.
defaultPrompt: Use chaos_feature to explain how this feature works.
Run chaos_add to update the index after my changes.
